text:
leo: noticed an onboarding hiccup in sample-kit where function/tool call outputs are double-encoded after an auth retry when using json-mode + streaming. customer hit it during integration tests.
anya: can you paste the minimal repro? short is fine.
leo: repro: 1) start streaming tool call in json-mode with preserveStrings=true 2) token refresh triggers retry while buffer holds raw chunks 3) retry wrapper re-serializes the buffered text, resulting in a quoted JSON string arriving at the validator
drew: i bet the retry layer assumes buffer is already JSON text and always does JSON.stringify. streamer preserved rawText so stringify on a string adds quotes.
leo: exact observed payload: '"{\"items\": [1,2,3]}"' instead of {"items":[1,2,3]}
anya: temporary fix idea: retry wrapper should inspect buffer type and only stringify if buffer is an object; if string and looksLikeJSON try safe-parse then resend. but that feels brittle.
drew: agreed. better is an explicit contract: StreamBuffer should expose getBufferedAsObject() and getBufferedAsText(). retry wrapper chooses which to use. that also makes node & py parity easier.
leo: proposing SDK helper signature for discussion:
```js
// in SDKs
replayBufferedToolCall(buffer, { format: 'object' | 'text' })
validateToolOutput(schema, { mode: 'strict' | 'coerce' | 'preserveStrings' })
```
anya: also add an integration test that simulates auth refresh mid-stream (auth-mock), assert that after retry consumer sees structured object when preserveStrings=false. run both runtimes in CI.
drew: opened draft PR with provisional parse-if-string guard for sample-kit to unblock customer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-kit/pull/1021. labelled WIP and will revert when we ship the contract.
sdk-bot: created issue #2738: "devex: define StreamBuffer contract and enforce retry replay parity across node+py" assigned to @anya
leo: ok i'll draft the spec doc and include example patches for node+py. want this landed before next sample-kit release to avoid more onboarding flickers.
anya: thanks, leo. i'll add parity tests to my queue. :thumbsup:
